meta_description: 6,168 likes, 67 comments - nigellalawson on October 20, 2026: "All roads lead to Rome — even in Melbourne!  I celebrated being back in this city for keen eaters at  @roma.melbourne, the restaurant Melburnians have been buzzing about recently, and it was even lovelier than I had dared hope. I had a moment of doorstep-doubt as I got lost in the vast office building it’s just off, but once in I knew I was safe — especially after I’d had a cupful of rich chickeny broth (pic 2), and was immersed in that most pleasurable of pursuits: The Reading of The Menu! As is proper for a Roman-inflected menu, there’s serious attention paid to offal, and I just had to have the brains, the creamy clouds battered and fried till crisp on the outside, the best of fritters, offset by a desirably sharp and briny green sauce with olives and capers (pic 3). And please, should you feel squeamish about this, don’t feel any compunction to announce it: I won’t make you eat them if you feel disinclined. I then had to try the nervetti all’arrabiata, the spicy tomato sauce pasta sauce here used as a dressing for beef tendons, cooked low and slow till they’re all jellied softness (pic 4). I’d never come across pasta alla Baronessa (pic 5) before, not even on Roman holidays, but the name lured me (shades of Sound of Music) along with the fact that this indicated a sauce of chicken livers and mushrooms — and very happy I was indeed with my order. I’m going to start making this when I’m home! It certainly was heaven here. The feast continued with a beautifully simple, perfectly cooked roast chicken,  gloriously bitter cima di rape and a seasonal vignarola, a sweet and salty stew of peas, lettuce, onions and guanciale(pic 1). I was certainly full up by this stage, but I knew I’d regret leaving without even a small scoop of their salted caramel ice cream (pic 6) and it was just gorgeously creamy and enliveningly salty. I adored it. But then, I adored all of it! And I also adore the portrait of that loveliest of chefs @mrwilkinsons in comedy porcine pose by his cabinet of pig heads, which you can see in pic 7. My final photo is a close up of their coaster, just for the joy of it. A properly swell evening out. Grazie Pino ed a tutti — laurel wreaths all round!".
